document.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Baker-Shevardnadze Ministerial in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. Second Small Group Meeting (Regional Issues), September 22, 1989
document.authors: U.S. Department of State (Bush Presidential Library)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: Yuri Alekseyev presents the Najibullah settlement plan: guiding council, monitored free elections, new constitution and an international conference with the US, USSR, Iran, Pakistan and China. Condoleezza Rice says the resistance would not accept the present government's composition; Baker says Najibullah's name should be taken off for the plan to fly.

events.description: Second small group meeting (regional issues) of the Baker-Shevardnadze ministerial, discussing Afghanistan among other topics.
Najibullah presented his plan for settlement (guiding council, loya jirga, elections, international conference).
Second small group meeting (regional issues) of Baker-Shevardnadze ministerial; discussion of Najibullah plan: guiding council, loya jirga, elections, international conference.
Baker suggested Najibullah's name be removed from the plan for it to have a chance; requested a written version of the plan.
Shevardnadze proposed a joint Soviet/American group go to Kabul; Baker joked it could also go to Tel Aviv.
Zoellick briefed on Central America (Tela accord, Esquipulas); Pavlov reported on working group results.
Dispute over Soviet arms supplies to Ethiopia; Shevardnadze rejected Baker's criticism and meeting adjourned.
Second small group meeting (regional issues) of the Baker-Shevardnadze ministerial covering Middle East, Cambodia, Afghanistan, Central America, Africa.
Najibullah presented his settlement plan, later reiterated at the non-aligned summit.
Alekseyev briefed on Najibullah's plan: guiding council, loya jirga, elections, international conference guaranteeing neutrality.
Rice stated that the US finds the transitional committee idea interesting but that the PDPA's composition blocks a solution.
Paris discussion approach on moratorium on arms supplies combined with internal settlement referenced.

key_claims: Soviet side presented Najibullah's plan (guiding council, loya jirga, elections, international conference) as a compromise showing no monopoly of power.
US said the PDPA's current composition blocked a cooperative solution and that the resistance would not deal with the Kabul government.
Baker suggested Najibullah's name be removed from the plan for it to have any chance.
Soviets noted that some resistance field commanders held bilateral talks with Kabul despite leaders' public refusal.
The Najibullah plan was a unilateral proposal not discussed with the resistance or the AIG.
Shevardnadze said Iran and India supported an international conference, Pakistan leaned in favor, China's position unknown.
Both sides agreed on a political settlement and neutral, non-aligned Afghanistan but diverged on details and an arms moratorium.
